written.myAnswer: Fungi are eukaryotic heterotrophs that absorb nutrients from decaying organic matter and have cell walls made of chitin. Most fungi are multicellular, but some, such as yeast, are unicellular.

Protista includes unicellular, colonial, filamentous or simple multicellular eukaryotes. Fungi are heterotrophic, absorb nutrients from decaying organic matter and have chitin cell walls. Plantae are multicellular autotrophs with cellulose cell walls that make food by photosynthesis. Animalia are multicellular heterotrophs that ingest and digest food within their bodies and lack cell walls.
